attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, said as his own position. He mentions Altman and Amodei only to dispute them.

semantics.note: Zitron said there is no 'proof'. The drafter wrote 'no evidence', which is a broader claim. Under 'no evidence', published estimates made before the post would count against him, but they do not count against 'no proof'. 'AI labs' is also broader than the OpenAI/Anthropic context. The contract fixes both problems.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: serving revenue minus the costs of serving, kept separate from training costs and net income. The proof standard is reasonable. Using 2025 as the period is the evaluator's choice. The contract tests the two parts of the claim separately, which allows a split result.

evidence.note: Independent Epoch AI estimate, public before the post. It puts the GPT-5 bundle's gross margin around 30%, with operating margin near break-even. It is a hedged estimate, so it is not proof and does not establish realized profit.
Amodei says his 50% figure was stylized and not about Anthropic. This backs Zitron's point that the figure is not proof, but it says nothing on actual profitability.

Audited 2025 S-1, filed before the evaluation date: revenue $4,585M, cost of revenue $2,773M (mostly compute for serving customers). Even if all $911M of sales and marketing (free-user compute, channel partners) is counted as serving cost, profit stays positive. It was not public at the time of the post, so it cannot show proof existed then.

reviews.rationale: Not profitable on inference: contradicted for Anthropic in 2025. Its audited filing shows a 39.5% gross margin, and serving profit stays positive (about $0.9B) even if all sales and marketing is counted as serving cost. No proof existed by March 31, 2026: this part holds on the packet. The pre-post material is an estimate (e1) and an executive's illustrative figure (e2), and the S-1 came out later. OpenAI realized figures are not established either way.
